The game is a lot of fun, until it stops being fun all of a sudden. Early on it can feel pretty easy, you're killing foot soldiers with your little dude, get a mech and can start going toe to toe with other mechs. You might die but it seems pretty fair. Then you get to the third area. It's mechs all the way down and they decided these guys need to be like ultra ace pilots that are constantly flying across the map faster than you can react. Try chasing them in your mech and oops you're suddenly exploded because it's almost impossible for you to hit them, but they can hit you easily. If you manage to beat the game, every gate miniboss becomes this kind of annoyance on subsequent runs, being a mach 3 gnat that suddenly swoops in with damage that wants to one-shot you while they can literally outrun your bullets. It wouldn't be so bad if they couldn't actually fly around in the air out of camera view 90% of the time making it almost impossible to keep a bead on them even with lockon. tldr: Fun game that decides to crank the difficulty from 1 to Dante Must Die with very little gradiance in-between

Fairly short for a roguelite and with little variation, but makes up for it with an extensive suite of between-run customization in the form of collecting passive skills, mecha parts, and weapons. The feel of any given weapon is more or less identical amongst all weapons of the same type, but what really got me was the way that different torsos and legs drastically change the feel of your movement due to their varied booster configurations and modes of locomotion, something I haven't really felt since the early Armored Core games. I'll be honest though, while Metal Bringer feels like it could have some serious depth to its combat, all of that goes out the window around Stage 3, where you hit a hard grind wall in the form of nigh-endless waves of enemy mechs, all utilizing a tier of parts higher than you've seen at that point in the game. The first few times you get there, you'll probably die within seconds, it's that brutal of a difficulty spike. It's at this point that Metal Bringer trips and falls on its face by forcing you to spend several runs simply grinding out defensive passives, which make Stage 3 possible, but also mitigate any further difficulty the game might have had, making subsequent floors, bosses, and even the entirety of NG+ a button mashing breeze that feels like a victory lap instead of a climax. Even the very concept of a cohesive build flies out the window at this point, as your stats will be so bloated and you'll have so many app disks and parts dropping that you'll accumulate virtually every skill in the game before you even reach the final boss (even the ones with tradeoffs), and still likely demolish everything in your path by simply holding dash and spamming attack. Afterwards, there's really nothing to do but... grind more, unlocking more parts and building cool mechs to steamroll the too-easy content. It's a bit disappointing, but I was also sort of expecting this to happen, given the nature of meta progression in these sorts of games. Overall though, I had fun, likely due to the fact that even with the grind, the game doesn't overstay its welcome. Besides, even after the difficulty spikes and then falls straight off a cliff, it's still a very pretty game with flashy visuals, and it offers excellent customization if you like building lil robot guys. Plus, it kinda scratches that musou itch, y'know? Recommended, though I suggest you play the demo first to see if the visuals gel with you, since as many negative reviews have mentioned, that nauseating pixel filter [i]cannot be turned off.[/i]

比起肉鸽更像是一个组build检验build的游戏，build在出击的那一刻就基本定了，局内成长基本不太能改变什么，你build好就能打得过，build差就是打不过。最大的优点也是在build成型后确实非常爽，机甲无双了说是。同时多样的武器及技能也能支持你尝试各种玩法，你可以全身装满浮游炮变身走路模拟器，你可以强化锁定速度和数量变身彩虹大炮锁一切，你可以双持黑洞炮全屏吸入。配上敌方时不时蹦出的各种萝卜动画名台词，玩起来确实十分热闹。 不过游戏节奏有点问题，特别是对射击流派而言，前两章掉落的装备技能乏善可陈，怎么组都差不太多，有趣的解锁都在第三章之后，然而第二章到第三章难度的差异也相当大，上来三台机甲堵门分分钟砍爆你。于是就陷入了一个神秘的怪圈：我打不过第三章怎么办？那你去刷第三章装备啊！我打不过第三章怎么刷第三章装备！玩家就只能反复刷前两章拿没什么意思的技能一点一点提升自己的强度，这段时间也确实很容易倦怠。而一旦你的实力到达了第三章的境界，游戏却又变得没什么难度了，基本可以一马平川推到结局。多样化的build变成了只是可以多样化无双的工具，我变强了，但是我又能打谁呢？ 除此之外，游戏的引导说明方面也有点问题，本来技能就很多了，说明文字又惜字如金，突出一个有没有用全凭感觉。比如“投掷武器”，说是某些近战武器攻击时会投掷武器。那么某些是哪些？你也不知道，结果一试好像只对动力兵武器有效；又比如“宛如流水”，说是垫步可以取消攻击，那么请问对机甲有没有效？答案是没有，因为机甲不能垫步；再比如你可知道武器附加火属性和冰属性会互相抵消，同时火属性会增加发热，冰属性则会降低温度，你也不知道，因为游戏里完全没告诉你。导致很多东西只能自己慢慢试出来，突出一个“探索感”，可能这就是魂味儿吧。 最后这游戏有些技能可以说是完全不知道拿来干啥的，不好说是设计还是翻译问题。比如一个技能又降射程又降攻击力，你说你装不装，那我打死也不装；又比如子弹反弹这个看起来非常有用的技能，结果你用激光武器的时候反弹的子弹能打到自己，突出一个伤人三千自损一万。好在游戏有锁定技能的功能，被坑一次锁了就算了( 总体来看，游戏的缺点在爽快度面前倒也可以容忍，如果本身就对机甲感兴趣的话还是挺推荐的，买来也可以爽刷个十几小时。

Please note that it's a completely subjective review of the game, and maybe I just don't understand some parts of the game. It's a pretty good game for it's price, but if we exclude price from consideration and think just about "fun", then it's not fun enough for me (even though I still play it occasionally to kill some time). There are a lot of good things in the game, but I'll focus on the bad parts. 1. Progression: You struggle in first floor until you oneshot everything. You get oneshot at floor 2. You struggle until you oneshot everything. You get oneshot at floor 3. I'm currently at floor 3, and it's kinda frustrating. And bosses are much weaker than hordes of Arms that appear on floors. Also, the fact that you don't even get a proper Arms at game start is so wrong in my opinion. 2. It feels like the devs are overcomplicating things in parts they should not. We can't even aim and lock on enemy Arms properly until we get the corresponding Apps. And there are too many Apps that should not even exist and should be just a part of ordinary gameplay from the very start. 3. Controls looks so complicated that devs even added 2 "default" presets for ranged and melee weapons, but I'm pretty sure you could make controls more simple without sacrificing anything. 4. Some weapons have pretty strange hitboxes that you miss a lot of enemies (until you start exploding everything with Apps lol). And the fact that you hurt yourself with your own ranged weapons is just weird. Maybe there's an App that disables self-harm, but I didn't find it among like 100 other Apps.... I'm only playing melee as a result. 5. Most mechanics get nullified with Apps. Why even add them in first place? Energy? Just regenerate energy from everything. Parts and weapons having separate life bars? Just regenerate life. Overheat/stun? Just stop getting overheat and stun (there are apps that increase damage while overheating and stuff, but it doesn't feel useful at my current stage at least for something like making an overheat build). This game doesn't feel "mecha" enough in the first place, and after some progression it loses everything "mecha" about it other than how your Arm looks. 6. Having the same hotkey for picking up Apps and rice balls as for moving to the next area is so annoying. I've traveled to the next area when trying to pick up an App at least 10 times already. Please make 2 separate hotkeys - one for picking up stuff and other for moving to the next area. 7. Arms with beam installed in their head part are annoying as hell. At floor 3 at least 3-4 of them spawn at the same time and just start stunlocking you. I think I could negate stunlock with some Apps, but it's a bad design in general, especially for a "slice through hordes of enemies like in musou" style game. 8. UI and sound/music are pretty bad. UI needs LOTS of QoL. Sounds like leveling up or weapon elemental effects are too annoying (especially because weapon effects are so loud and music is almost non-existent during fights). The most annoying thing so far is when you analyze Apps or do a OS tuning, you get spammed by annoying loud sounds (and the animation for it is too long). 9. I feel like adding special attacks when you have the same weapon type equipped in both arms is a mistake. From my personal experience, there's little sense to equip anything other than 2 of the same weapons at once. It's kinda fun at start, but it becomes way too repetitive. Maybe there are special attacks and combos when you have different weapons equipped, but it's way different from EVERY attack being a joint attack with both weapons. 10. It's so weird that the game starts microfreezing and stuttering at floor 3 even on my 4080 Super. I guess I should turn raytracing off, but it's just a bad design for a "retro style game". Ideally players shouldn't even think about these things and just play the game and have fun. 11. I'm a Front Mission and Armored Core fan, so not having shoulder weapon types is kinda weird for me :D You can get an Arm that holds 4 weapons, but you can only equip 4 "arm" weapon types and switch them. 12. There are a lot of things the game doesn't tell you about at all, like mechanics and stuff. It would be ok if it was much more simple, but, as I said, it's overcomplicated in a lot of things.

时隔千年，少女丝莉雅从冷冻睡眠中苏醒过来，此时全世界陷入了智械危机，外面到处都是机器人叛军，作为目前唯一的人类，她与搭档机器人拍档仔携手组装出人型仿生机器人“动力兵”，踏上了一边寻找其他幸存人类，一边揪出罪魁祸首的旅途。 别看商店界面里写着《机兵大乱战》是一款Roguelite动作游戏，其实本作包含肉鸽要素并不多，主要体现在每次场景切换、敌人配置以及掉落物不同罢了。在游玩方面，它其实更偏向于无双刷子类动作砍杀，主打的一边爽一边肝的体验。 [h1]哪里爽[/h1] 如果你玩过《侍神大乱战》，你就会发现这两款游戏竟是如此的相似。没错，这两款游戏都出自于ALPHAWING Inc.之手。第一眼看上去像是像素，实际上采用的是3D模型实时渲染成像素画面的技术，并在此基础上引入光线追踪，使得光影效果很出色。机甲战斗时的金属反光、爆炸火光以及粒子特效在此风格下呈现出独一份的层次感，画面表现华丽，这也形成了该团队独有的视觉辨识度。不过在敌人与攻击特效众多时，如此画面也容易导致场面混乱，以致于玩家难以看清敌人的攻击和弹幕，以及自身位置，这也是为什么不少人说玩久了容易头晕的关系。不过也受益于这种“眼花缭乱”的炫丽画面加上对战时各种五颜六色数字特效，结合“拳拳到机”的打击音效，让游戏玩起来有种莫名其妙的爽快感，就像在玩无双割草游戏般，到后期数字膨胀后，这一感觉更是越发的明显。 [h1]哪里肝[/h1] 游戏内置非常多有着能增加被动数值的不同app插件，以及涉及身体、腿部、左武器和右武器四个部位机甲部件可以解锁（不同机甲武器的攻击范围、速度与特效各异，涉及武器种类丰富，共26种武器，近战远程都有），机甲部件之间的随机搭配，加之自由涂色改装的DIY系统（从性能到外观设计，均可进行细致的定制），可玩性很强。不过解锁这些部件基本上都需要花费不少的D晶片（D晶片还能用于局外成长，提升角色生命、防御以及机甲各项性能，强化选项多达 40 项），然而前期靠刷获得D晶片的效率又很低，所以这个过程难免少不了肝。简单提示一下，游戏内含成就系统，完成对应的成就可以获取D晶片,数量不少，建议前期尽可能地先去刷成就。 最后不得不吐槽下，该作教程做得实在是太简陋了，除了基本的移动和攻击外，其余重要的信息居然一个字不提，以至于不理解的玩家刚开始玩的时候极易走弯路，所以我在这里简单罗列一下你游玩前应该知道的两点事情： 1.地图上每个房间里的敌人都刷不完，随时可以去往到下一个房间（打够一定数量的图会出精英关卡）； 2.玩家在场景内获得的app插件跟机甲部件，在结束任务退出后会重置，并不能带走。需要在一路上遇到的技能商店跟机甲商店里花钱解析，解析后才能永久解锁，在下一次游玩的时候就能进行自定义编辑了。 [quote] 加入[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/ADZZW]爱の榨汁屋[/url]&关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/34815366/]爱の鉴赏家[/url]，用爱品鉴世间作品，用心流淌真情实感。 [/quote]

I played this game on stream, the link to my first impressions is at the bottom of this review. Overall, I think it's a cool idea, and I think there is potential to get into it if you are willing to give it the time, but it also has a lot of glaring problems that really made me bounce off it quick. To begin, the controls were mapped by an alien, wanting some sort of two-handed keyboard control scheme, while also still mapping camera move movement to the mouse, basically requiring a third arm. I highly recommend anyone playing on keyboard mouse to remap the controls as soon as possible. That said, a small but rather annoying design decision was that the main menu couldn't be opened during a level. This means mapping keys can only be done outside of the runs, which I argue is when you need to map keys the least; you are least likely to think about it then and least likely to find your current mapping wanting. The game itself presents a lot of complexity, though I wonder if it's complex because of a layer of interpretation you have to do with it's own vocabulary or if it truly actually is complex. Either way, initial impressions make it feel rather overwhelming all the options and choices you have. I think to me - and this is very much a matter of opinion - but I feel like the rogue-like structure really holds this back. I think a well crafted game that relied less on luck and with a linear flow of progression would have been far more satisfying - especially with the mech crafting thing. As it is, it's just another rogue-like in the endless glut of indie rogue-likes that, while to some extent offers some permanent progression after each run, it still overly relies on luck to determine your overall success and therefore enjoyment with the game. To that end, I felt disappointed with this one. If you'd like to watch my experience with the game, the link is below: https://www.youtube.com/live/eYp8VZ4evrM?si=oevFsXFF_MRFVA8l

First off: if you want a solid customization-focused mecha game and can look past the jank, DEFINITELY BUY THIS. There's a lot to love but I'm leaving a negative review based on some crippling first impressions in hope it's more visible to the publisher. This may change as I play more. [h3]The Good[/h3] Insane customization, exactly what I want to see in a mecha game. There's 26 weapon types grouped into classes but even in classes they have slightly different behaviors. Every weapon I've found so far has been fun to use and has a niche it excels in. Tons of head/leg parts with different mobility options and a choice between light frames with 2 weapons vs heavier frames with 2x2 weapons. The combat is simple but satisfying. It feels inspired by the trend of wave-survival roguelites popularized by Vampire Survivors. It does a great job setting itself apart with the active, engaging mech combat. You mow through waves of mooks for resources and then fight simple but engaging bosses with neat gimmicks. The upgrade system is also very satisfying and avoids many common roguelite pitfalls. There are two main types of upgrade. "OS Tuning" affects base stats/proficiency and increases based on your playstyle but you can also spend currency to level them manually. "Apps" are skills, each has a point cost taken from a pool. These are the major, gameplay-affecting upgrades which range from "gain more currency" to "add new moves to a combo" to "completely change how a weapon plays". I like that the progression sets itself apart from most roguelites. Almost all progress is incremental and persistent, though you will be scavenging enemy parts a lot in early runs. You aren't at the mercy of RNG to get the things you need to win, instead unlocking more content the further you survive that helps in your next run. [h3]The Bad[/h3] The camera sucks. This is the top complaint in every negative review and I fully agree. It's not unplayable by any means but the controls are... unconventional. R-stick pans, bumpers turn. There's only two vertical camera angles. I believe this is to emphasize the pseudo-isometric artstyle, but it hurts the game too much. I'd much prefer a traditional R-stick orbiting camera. The camera has a tendency of auto-panning to a priority target. Thankfully this is the one behavior that CAN be turned off, but many players may not know that unless they dig in the settings. The artstyle is great, but the pixel shader's default cell size is way too big. It can be nearly impossible to figure out what's going on in a busy fight, especially on lower resolutions. The ability to configure the cell size or turn the shader off entirely would be huge. The lack of a floor-wide map is crippling. You can see your current room in full with map markers for sites of interest, but each floor can be maze-like. Some unusual room connections make it hard to figure out where you are. Most floors have multiple exits so you'll typically stumble on one of them, but clearing entire floors and their gate bosses requires memorizing the layout. Apps don't tell you what they do until you analyze (pay to unlock) them. I can only imagine this is intentional, but it's a questionable choice. The first few batches you unlock will matter the most and their prices make this expensive experimentation. Likewise, there isn't much of a stat display in general so it can be hard to weigh what apps/OS upgrades you should invest in. This one's probably just me but the song that plays in the intro/lobby is grating... the soundtrack overall is quite good but that one track is rough on the ears :') Also, I discovered an annoying bug where the game can softlock if you open one of the D-pad menus while exiting your Arms. Luckily you just have to restart and it keeps your progress. [h3]Overall[/h3] Buy it if you want a mecha game with a ton of customization and/or if you like wave-based roguelites with lots of unlockable content. The current 30% off sale is a steal, full price is questionable. Beware that there is jank which may or may not be fixed, especially with the camera.

[h1]A Mecha sized Mess[/h1] To understand what makes Metal Bringer not something I recommend we need to look at ALPHAWINGS previous game : Samurai Bringer. Samurai Bringer, similar in perspective and control, has a very curious system in its core ; the move list editor. While clunky in use and lacking a proper preview of any sorts it is the main appeal of that game. Constructing your own moves and weaving those into your combos lists is something completely unique in video games so this is the only game to take that throne. (Maybe Fighter Maker but that is way more of game/meme making tool rather than an actual game) Metal Bringer lacks that or anything remotely enticing. Sure, build-your-own-mech is the cool stuff [b]I[/b] can't get enough off (that is if it isnt just the stoic Gundam or 20km turning radius of Battletech fame). This has been done both better and worse before and is merely a [b]fragile[/b] piece of this game. There is also the chip system which act as build identity, calibration and tuning... with [b]complete of lack an immediately visible or accessable stat screen?![/b] But thats the type of clunkyness that made it over that you really dont want now because now you have to test your mech and starts off being [b]ON FIRE[/b] for petes sake. Entering a new run: a fine Twin-stick shooter with some optional vertically. Some very out of place take-a-break-puzzles. You move through rooms one by one without any backtracking and without much of any idea whats next. There are part repair and chip shops on the way which also give you the much needed opportunity to permanently unlock the collected pieces into your garage and a new run. This is a pain. Leaving and reentering for every single piece you want. The lack of funds will force you to retrive all the achivement rewards. The worlds most grating [b]"YOU NOW HAVE THIS PERMANENT!!"[/b] jingle... You need to do all of this though. Each stage gets more wild at a pace that you are not going to out rougelike it. Meta-progression upgrades are key. You cannot build a strategy mid-run, [b]obliterating the rougelike aspect.[/b] Enemy mechs [u]can[/u] drop their parts for you to equip, complete with annoyances like : hold button to pickup, left/right arms are not interchangeable, each piece has HP and : no legs = no mech. Yes, you can move out without a mech. This is a death wish though as it takes even less to kill your tiny robot pilot body and end your run. Because even if you do have your optimized well oiled machine, it [b]will[/b] break into pieces if something just looks at it funny. Your equipped and collected chips will still work fine and you will need them. But the Danmaku levels of fragilty is so infuriating when the battlefield grows into such a mess and you are a such sizeable target. Double if its your own creation. Triple because you must now readjust due to [u]gameplay mutilation[/u]. Just because you can do that easily with a mech doesn't make it a good idea in a video game and that isn't even news. Ugggh... So you will likely need to scramble pieces together anyway. [b]ON the damn battlefield[/b]. Menuing through anything remotely useful. For next time. Managing part HP, Energy, Overheat, Overcool (Yes that is a thing too). Getting almost oneshot every step of the run. Presentation wise : The over-retro visuals are neat. Unlocked internal resolution would look great. Sound is bland. Music is lacking, particually the main theme is ass. Seriously hire some tracker-wizards. Framerate can dip really bad at times. You may call it [b]Armored Core Pocket[/b] or [b]Grand Theft Mech[/b] but either way it aint that good.

[h1]玩到真正的机甲游戏了 [/h1] 《机兵大乱战》是一款带有肉鸽元素的动作游戏。别看游戏的画面是像素风，但它对机甲细节的展示以及机甲对战的场景确实要比不少3D游戏还要精彩，再加上无双割草的乐趣和与强敌对战的激烈，甚至还能跳跃出一个Z轴实现空中躲避等精彩操作，实在是能给人带来不断的惊喜。 [h2]故事简介 [/h2] 女主丝莉雅因为“星球再生计划”在冷冻仓里沉睡了1000年，等她醒来后世界已经大变样。为了寻找自己的亲人和其他同样休眠的人类，她在搭档仔机器人的建议下接管了仿生机器人“动力兵”的管理权限，操纵它们探索外面的世界寻找人类的踪迹。 [h2]游戏玩法 [/h2] 这是一款将无双和动作肉鸽结合起来的游戏，每张地图都有超多的敌人，玩家的每个攻击都能打倒一大片，所以爽感是肯定是不缺的，一些关卡还会遇到精英机甲敌人，在击败它们后我们可以穿上它们的机甲部件继续推进关卡。BOSS的话有一定难度，不是最开始的我们能够打败的，那种巨型BOSS给人的压迫感很强，很难想象一个像素画风的游戏能做把动画做到这么的惊喜。 [h2]养成部分 [/h2] 因为敌人数值会变高，所以玩家必须要要有提升各项能力的手段，所以肝等级肝材料肝部件是这个游戏最肝的部分。特别是部件获取后一定要去维修站解析，不然不能解锁，甚至在机甲部件被损毁后无法再次拾取，所以这个部分操作是有点繁琐的，但因为养成部分把游戏时间拉的很长，碰运气也能回收很多机甲部件。 [h2]机甲爱好者[/h2] 游戏制作组应该很喜欢机甲元素，因为这游戏的细节部分已经超过了许多机甲游戏的大作。首先是机甲部件可以混搭，共有基座、机体和左臂右臂四个部件，其中左臂右臂代表近战和远程两种武器，基座会影响驾驶速度，这些都是上手就能体会到的。至于升级的内容也和这些有关，比如降低能耗，或者增加两种武器的攻击力，虽然前期不明显，等升到一定等级之后能感受到攻击和制空的时间明显延长，这就给打BOSS创造了更多的窗口期，可以体会到更爽快的攻防战。 [h2]总结 [/h2] 作为一款机甲游戏，《机兵大乱战》确实在机体设计、部件涂装等方面做得很不错，虽然是像素风，但也能看到各个部件的细节，这点在战斗过程中也有体现。玩法是动作肉鸽和无双割草的融合，打BOSS的环节不用说，可以给到夯，但是打小兵的话主要看玩家能不能接受无双玩法，毕竟这个部分打的时间长了还是容易腻的。这游戏非常我更倾向于推荐给机甲游戏爱好者，毕竟这个肝部件升等级的过程确实要很久，唯有耐心的玩家才能体会收集全机甲的乐趣。 [quote] 闲暇时光，不妨试试游戏。 欢迎关注[url=store.steampowered.com/curator/45653622/] 闲暇時光鉴赏组 [/url] [/quote]

[i] 天空一碧如洗、蔽日穿云、无边无垠…… 这番话是出自何人之口呢……？ 喔喔，我记得，这是楼陀罗所提到的假想现实……类似于童话故事 人类躲进地下都市避难，究竟已经过了多少年了呢？ 见过蓝天的人，如今也已经一个不剩了 现在的我，被关在一个无机质的墙壁中，又低、又窄 我究竟是从什么时候开始处于这里的呢…… [/i] 《机兵大乱战》是一款融合了“拼好机”、无双割草与Roguelite的像素风动作游戏。人类面临无法生存的困境，无奈之下选择运用冷冻技术集体沉睡到千年后的世界。但觉醒的人工智能『湿婆』背叛了人类，极力阻止人类从沉睡中苏醒……少女丝莉雅成为了人类最后的王牌。DIY出风格独特的动力兵、驾驶重型机甲出战、将沿途的杂兵们尽数毁灭吧！迎战强大的boss，贯彻“拿来主义”，不断用敌人的部件改装机甲、增强战力！ 作为一个资深颜狗，本作吸引我的当然是其独特的画风啦😋很久以前，我对像素风游戏的印象还是“画风简陋/为了节省经费”，即使现在已经有很多表现出不俗视觉效果的像素游戏，像《Hyper Light Drifter》、《REPLACED》都是其中的翘楚，多次刷新了我对于像素游戏的认知，但当我看到本作中竟然能靠像素展现出动漫一般的流畅度和质感，还是为此惊讶不已。 前面提到，本作某种意义上算是割草游戏，而在像素和复古电子音乐的加持下，如同动漫中龙傲天主人公一样打遍天下无敌手、每一次挥刀都撂倒一片敌人，爽感这块给得足足的。此外，小兵们退场时还会像灰太狼那样喊口号，比如“一个我倒下去，千千万万个站起来！”和“年轻人，不讲武德”等等，非常诙谐幽默。 而本作的核心机制：拼好兵，则在第一次看到大乱斗时有一个简短的“试用期”，试用过后我们就只能用回最基础的叉车了。每一次击毁敌方机甲，我们都能拾取四肢与武器——什么大刀长枪钻头霰弹枪加特林等等应有尽有，甚至还有能够飞天的喷气推进式腿部！所有部件即捡即用，当场更换，型号限制？不存在的！即使没有注意过热、过度使用而损坏了武器也无妨，捡个新部件一装，又是一条好汉。 总体而言，《机兵大乱战》是一部爽感十足的作品，不过有一说一指引的部分非常一般，理想中的指引应当是循序渐进在关卡进行中慢慢引入，而不是丢一本厚如小字典的术语指南，让玩家逐个查阅自行理解。说起来开发组的新作《侍神大乱战: 纵横天下》即将发售，不知道这个问题在新作中是否有所改善？让我们拭目以待。 [quote] 奏游戏之乐章，品人生之绚烂 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45672460/]欢迎加入 『 丰川集团 』[/url] [u][b]以丰川集团之名，行评测鉴赏之事[/b][/u][/quote]

Great game overall, the variety in mech parts, weapons, and app modifiers really change your playstyle in a meaningful and substantial ways, so it gets the main part of why rogue-lites are good by not having a shallow system, that feels the same each run. The customization is certainly a highlight, treading between Armored core and Custom Robo levels of fine tuning. The combat is great, giving unique move sets for every melee weapon type and a unique moveset for if you are dual wielding the same weapons too; There is also a matching level of thought put into the movesets for the little pilot as well, so every aspect of combat is pretty well thought out; It's not DMC or Bayo levels of complex, but it's certainly a cut above your typical hack and slash or Souls-like game. It's satisfying doing combos, shooting, blowing everything up, and becoming stronger. The rogue lite elements definitely let you become more OP if you use the right combo of apps and just play more to increase your collection. So even if you are bad at the game, you'll eventually level your character with OS tunings to be more survivable, which also increases your capacity for how many apps you can have installed. Now for the Bad, which there aren't many things to list, but it's a problem nonetheless for me. 1: The Music sucks hard, it's generic, monotonous chiptune sounding rubbish that has no soul in my opinion (There are definitely thousands of good examples of quality chiptune music, this just sucks though). So I definitely recommend using another game's playlist in the background while playing. I had various electronic themed game OSTs playing in the background like Einhander, One step from Eden, BallisticNG, and Assault Spy. 2: The visuals settings don't give you the option to turn off the pixel filter, which I don't even think looks very good the way they implemented it. The low poly 3d models would look fine on their own, so I think it's just a poorly executed visual gimmick. Still waiting for someone to make a mod that removes the pixelation, but this game is a year old already so I don't think that is happening. Also the explosions and other VFX can cause big frame drops if a lot of them are happening at once, even on my rig with the game limiting framerates to 120fps maximum. 3: Lack of Statistical Transparency. Metal Bringer does that annoying gormless developer thing where they don't give you specific and accurate numbers for your stats when customizing your builds, i.e. "X App Raises or lowers your attack or defense", but they never give you an amount, just a vague notion that said stat, moved one way or another. No idea why they did this since the Mechs do have pretty detailed stats and visuals for how their movement and thrusters are calculated, but nothing for how Apps influence your total stats on anything. 4: No savable Equipment/Build sets. You can't make and save equipment sets to quickly swap between playstyles before you go on a run. This is mainly a problem when it comes to your App customization since that dictates what playstyle and equipment you'll want to be running every time, i.e. Melee focused, gun focused, solid dmg, beam damage, defensive, apps, offensive glass canon apps, etc... Ideally you'd be able to conveniently swap between all these like most action rpg games with this level of customization (like monster hunter). All in all I still recommend Metal Bringer and perhaps this review has informed you enough to know whether or not this game will be to your liking. I hope AlphaWIng makes another game like this but bigger and better down the line and fixes all my complaints in their next entry.

Normally I would play a little longer before posting a review, but this game is so sludge-like to play, I can't bring myself to it. I notice most negative reviews are about the bugs, so I'll talk about the gameplay. It's a completely miserable roguelike if you're trying to play it and not button-mash around with your brain off. Your run is, the first few times, dictated by what you find. Both your Labor (the giant robot) and your android avatar. Weapons have little to no meaningful difference in how they play. You essentially have three kinds: 1) Melee 2) Fast ranged 3) Slow ranged The animations for melee weapons come in two kinds: thrusting and spinning. Thrusts are (situationally) good for bigger Labors, spinning is (generally) good for mobs. Explosives (slow ranged) can be good against both, but without proper mods you're likely to miss shots, and even with mods you can still miss. Fast ranged attacks suffer a similar problem unless you're completely up Labor enemy asses, or a half a block away from smaller mobs. Most of the mods (apps) are obnoxious small percentage bonuses to random stats. You'll be balancing things like "+1% to thunder defense damage" or "+1% thunder damage on attacks". A few of the apps are useful on paper, but poor in execution, such as bullet speed. Even fewer are apps that are good in execution and worthwhile. You spend coins on most everything in the game. Analyzing parts lets you take them with you on the next run, and this includes apps and Labor parts. Over time you're likely to build a specific machine you want, and you're less likely to work with whatever you find in the game. Meaning the more you play this roguelike, the less rogue it becomes, which is bizarre design. The game also has the habit of many roguelites where you need to unlock things like movement speed or jump skills, so the first few hours of play is a complete slog and feels like ass. This isn't the sort of game where that gets better quickly unless you happen to come across the "game doesn't feel like walking through buckets of horse semen" app. The default camera and controls are also designed to frustrate. Despite playing slow, the game has you zoomed in far too close with an abysmal FOV. The level design also puts a lot of things like buildings, bridges, and trees in between your character and the camera. You can turn on the option to highlight your character, but it's small comfort when the overly pixelated aesthetic makes the amorphous blob of your avatar hard to read. Are you facing forward or backwards? How high is your character? Are you in an attack animation or jump animation, or has it ended? Who knows? Who cares? Clearly not PLAYISM. All of that, of course, could be waved away, tolerated even, if the way to acquire mech parts wasn't so very against the very nature of the game. Let me explain, the draw of Metal Bringer is that you can customize your mech, the Labor, BUT that requires gaining Labor parts from enemies. First, downing an enemy isn't a guarantee you'll get a part, and often you'll be fighting several Labors at once, so when a piece finally drops you might not be able to use it right away. THEN, if the enemy is defeated, AND you can equip the part (just because you have a Labor doesn't mean you can use a part), you have to contend with the part likely being broken as all get out. If you want to repair it you'll need to find one of the random repair shops and happen to be carrying a fat stack of money to repair it. If you get hit by any one of a hundred bullets or mobs (made hard to distinguish because of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ aesthetic) there's a real chance your new part will break. Can you go back and get the old part? No, of course not. When you go to a new map that's it, you can't go back. So, we have a roguelite game that absolutely does not want to be played like a rogue game. You have to grind to make it playable, everything is hard to make out and sluggish so you need to mash buttons, and you're always better off not trying new builds or options. I haven't even gotten into the completely boring and lazy world building, where the whitest girl in history fights an idiot's concept of Hindu beings (I say beings because gods, monsters, and demigods are all thrown together based on visual aesthetics, and in no way make logical sense). Imagine a christian mecha game where the bosses are the archangel Michael, Dante, Beelzebub, and the Virgin Mary. It sounds cool, only because of how stupid it is. Seeing how precious the country of India is over how Hinduism is represented, I how the government of India arrests the devs and breaks their hands with bricks for wasting my time on this idiot zone of a game.
